stated_failure_reason: Trial halted — patients showed worsening cognition and increased skin cancer risk vs placebo
mechanistic_assessment: gamma-secretase cleaves multiple substrates beyond amyloid including Notch which is essential for immune and gut signaling. Blocking it caused Notch-related toxicity invisible in mouse models. Drug may also have trapped Abeta inside cells rather than reducing it.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target pathway active in humans silent in model
notes: Multi-substrate target — pleiotropic enzyme collateral effects

stated_failure_reason: No significant cognitive improvement over placebo in Phase 3
mechanistic_assessment: Drug successfully cleared amyloid plaques but clearing amyloid did not improve cognition. Amyloid is likely a downstream marker not the upstream cause. Irreversible neuronal loss had already occurred before treatment.
ontology_category: B2 - Biomarker cleared but disease mechanism unaffected
notes: Canonical example of biomarker-outcome decoupling in neurodegeneration

stated_failure_reason: Did not meet primary cognitive endpoint in mild-to-moderate AD
mechanistic_assessment: Same root failure as bapineuzumab — modifying amyloid did not produce clinical benefit. A dedicated mild-patient trial also failed confirming amyloid hypothesis insufficient as sole driver.
ontology_category: B2 - Biomarker cleared but disease mechanism unaffected
notes: Third confirmation of amyloid hypothesis failure

stated_failure_reason: No significant effect on cognition or daily activities in Phase 3
mechanistic_assessment: Phase 2 benefit was artifact — placebo arm declined faster than expected creating false positive. Drug had poor brain penetration and never reached therapeutic CNS concentrations. Worked in young mice but failed in aged mice.
preclinical_model_used: Tg2576 mice tested in young animals only
ontology_category: C2 - Model too young to predict human disease-stage reality
notes: Phase 2 false positive driven by statistical artifact not biological signal

stated_failure_reason: Did not slow cognitive or functional decline in mild-to-moderate AD
mechanistic_assessment: Tau accumulation in moderate AD may be too advanced to reverse. Drug hit its target but intervening at this disease stage had no clinical benefit. Timing problem not a target problem.
ontology_category: E3 - Enrolled at wrong disease stage
notes: Early-stage tau intervention may still be valid

stated_failure_reason: No clinical benefit — trial stopped early with slight cognitive worsening
mechanistic_assessment: Drug powerfully reduced Abeta. Still no cognitive benefit and caused slight worsening. BACE1 has essential functions beyond amyloid processing including synaptic plasticity and myelination — disrupting these caused harm.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target pathway active in humans underweighted in model
notes: Confirmed amyloid reduction insufficient and revealed BACE1 pleiotropic function as risk

stated_failure_reason: Did not slow cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's
mechanistic_assessment: Designed at lower doses to avoid ARIA brain swelling but doses too low to adequately clear amyloid. Safety-efficacy tradeoff unresolved preclinically.
ontology_category: D3 - Dose required for efficacy incompatible with human safety
notes: Safety-driven dose reduction created efficacy gap not tested preclinically

stated_failure_reason: Inconsistent results across two Phase 3 trials — one positive one negative
mechanistic_assessment: Phase 2 showed amyloid clearance. Phase 3 contradictory results reflect patient population heterogeneity. Amyloid clearance alone unreliable surrogate for cognitive benefit.
ontology_category: E1 - Patient heterogeneity masked by small Phase 2 population
notes: Controversial FDA approval — illustrates how Phase 2 small samples mask heterogeneity

stated_failure_reason: Excess deaths in treatment arm — trial terminated early
mechanistic_assessment: Two failures: off-target aldosterone activation raised blood pressure. More fundamentally epidemiological HDL-cardiovascular correlation was mistaken for causal mechanism. Raising HDL artificially does not replicate protective biology of naturally high HDL.
ontology_category: B1 - Epidemiological correlation mistaken for causal mechanism
notes: Torcetrapib also had compound-specific aldosterone toxicity on top of class-level hypothesis failure

stated_failure_reason: No clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefit despite raising HDL
mechanistic_assessment: Clean CETP inhibition with no off-target blood pressure problem. Still no benefit. Confirmed target hypothesis itself was wrong not the compound.
ontology_category: B1 - Epidemiological correlation mistaken for causal mechanism
notes: Cleanest proof that CETP hypothesis was wrong at target level not compound level

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy — no reduction in cardiovascular events
mechanistic_assessment: Third confirmation that CETP inhibition raises HDL but does not reduce heart attacks. Target hypothesis empirically falsified across three independent compounds.
ontology_category: B1 - Epidemiological correlation mistaken for causal mechanism
notes: By this point the class failure was predictable from two prior failures

stated_failure_reason: No better than placebo — increased seizure and stroke risk
mechanistic_assessment: A1 receptors in kidney were sound hypothesis. But A1 receptors also present in brain — blocking caused seizures and excess strokes. Rodent brains handle A1 blockade differently than humans.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target CNS pathway active in humans underweighted in model
notes: CNS A1 receptor biology is species-specific — preclinical models systematically underweight this

stated_failure_reason: Trial terminated — excess cardiovascular hospitalizations and deaths
mechanistic_assessment: Drug raised GFR as expected but GFR rise was hemodynamic not functional — kidney filtering harder not healthier. Masked cardiovascular strain. Rodent cardiovascular physiology differs substantially from human.
ontology_category: D1 - Biomarker improved by non-disease mechanism
notes: Classic hemodynamic GFR artifact — biomarker looked like efficacy in both species but meant different things biologically

stated_failure_reason: Did not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events vs placebo
mechanistic_assessment: Lp-PLA2 is a marker of plaque inflammation but not a driver of plaque rupture. Inhibiting it reduced enzyme activity but did not change event rates.
preclinical_model_used: Rabbit atherosclerosis models plus epidemiological data
ontology_category: B1 - Epidemiological correlation mistaken for causal mechanism
notes: Epidemiological association between Lp-PLA2 and CV events was robust but non-causal

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed to show improvement in progression-free or overall survival
mechanistic_assessment: Iniparib was not a true PARP inhibitor. Post-failure biochemistry showed it worked through non-specific cysteine modification. Phase 2 showed real activity from wrong mechanism making Phase 3 patient selection incorrect.
preclinical_model_used: Triple-negative breast cancer cell lines and xenograft mouse models
ontology_category: A2 - Drug mechanism mischaracterized preclinically
notes: Canonical example of mechanism mischaracterization — Phase 2 success was real but from wrong target

stated_failure_reason: Failed to demonstrate improvement in time to disease progression
mechanistic_assessment: ETA blocking works in cell lines but prostate cancer is heterogeneous — only a subset have high ETA pathway dependence. Broad enrollment diluted any signal from responders.
preclinical_model_used: Human prostate cancer cell lines and xenograft models in immunodeficient mice
ontology_category: E1 - Broad enrollment diluted signal from true responder subpopulation
notes: Endothelin pathway still valid in ETA-high subgroup — stratification failure not target failure

stated_failure_reason: Did not improve overall survival in Phase 3 melanoma trial
mechanistic_assessment: Bcl-2 is one of many anti-apoptotic proteins. Melanoma cells upregulated other survival pathways when Bcl-2 was blocked. Pathway redundancy not captured in cell line models.
preclinical_model_used: Melanoma cell lines genetically homogeneous single-pathway dominant
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but disease driven by redundant parallel pathways
notes: Early example of Bcl-2 family redundancy — later led to BH3 mimetics targeting multiple family members

stated_failure_reason: Did not meet primary endpoint in Phase 2/3 lung cancer trial
mechanistic_assessment: HSP90 essential for normal cells too. Therapeutic window between killing cancer and damaging normal tissue too narrow. Cancer cell selectivity in cell lines was less pronounced in human patients with intact immune systems.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models in immunodeficient mice
ontology_category: C3 - Immunodeficient model removed immune and stromal context
notes: HSP90 class has struggled broadly — narrow therapeutic index is a consistent class problem

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient clinical activity across multiple solid tumor trials
mechanistic_assessment: RAS requires farnesylation to work — correct hypothesis. But when farnesyltransferase blocked RAS switches to alternative lipid modification that also activates it. Escape mechanism present but underappreciated in early cell work.
preclinical_model_used: Cell lines with RAS mutations and xenograft models
ontology_category: B3 - Compensatory escape mechanism not captured in model
notes: Geranylgeranylation escape is a fundamental limitation of the entire farnesyltransferase inhibitor class

stated_failure_reason: Did not extend progression-free survival
mechanistic_assessment: PKC-beta is one node in complex signaling network. Blocking it alone insufficient — other kinase pathways compensated. Preclinical models used cell lines with artificially high PKC-beta dependency not representative of patients.
preclinical_model_used: Lymphoma cell lines with high PKC-beta activity
ontology_category: C1 - Homogeneous model not representative of patient population
notes: Model selection bias — chose cell lines that confirmed hypothesis

stated_failure_reason: Limited efficacy and significant liver and GI toxicity
mechanistic_assessment: Formulation required Cremophor EL solvent that itself causes toxicity. Narrow therapeutic window. Clean preclinical activity did not account for solvent toxicity in human systemic administration.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft mouse models
ontology_category: F1 - Off-target formulation toxicity not visible in model
notes: Formulation-driven toxicity is underappreciated — solvent effects rarely tested preclinically

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient response rate in elderly AML patients
mechanistic_assessment: Same fundamental problem as lonafarnib — RAS switches to geranylgeranylation as escape. AML driven by diverse mutations beyond RAS — patients not selected for RAS pathway dependence.
preclinical_model_used: AML cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: E2 - Responder biomarker not identified preclinically
notes: Two independent farnesyltransferase inhibitors failed via same mechanism — strong ontology signal

stated_failure_reason: Trial stopped — increased deaths in treatment arm with no efficacy signal
mechanistic_assessment: IGF-1R blocking disrupts insulin regulation causing hyperglycemia more severe in humans than mice. IGF-1R role in cancer maintenance smaller than cell line studies suggested.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target metabolic effects more severe in humans than model
notes: Insulin/IGF-1 axis disruption systematically underweighted in xenograft models lacking metabolic complexity

stated_failure_reason: Did not improve survival in non-small cell lung cancer
mechanistic_assessment: PKC-alpha is one of many survival kinases in NSCLC. Patients not selected for PKC-alpha pathway dependence. Antisense delivery to solid tumors less efficient than in cell culture.
preclinical_model_used: NSCLC cell lines with limited xenograft data
ontology_category: E2 - Responder biomarker not identified — unselected patient population
notes: Antisense delivery efficiency gap between cell culture and solid tumor is a recurring problem

stated_failure_reason: No improvement in overall survival in Phase 3
mechanistic_assessment: AKT is one of most redundant nodes in cancer signaling — multiple ways to maintain survival when AKT blocked. Colorectal cancer patients not selected for PI3K pathway activation.
preclinical_model_used: Colorectal cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: E1 - Unselected population combined with pathway redundancy
notes: AKT inhibition without patient selection is now recognized as insufficient across most tumor types

stated_failure_reason: Did not improve overall survival in higher-risk MDS
mechanistic_assessment: Rigosertib true mechanism of action was contested — later shown to work differently than claimed binding RAS-binding domains rather than direct kinase inhibition. Mechanism mischaracterization led to wrong patient selection.
preclinical_model_used: MDS and AML cell lines and mouse xenograft models
ontology_category: A2 - Drug mechanism mischaracterized preclinically
notes: Mechanism debate persisted even after failure — illustrates how imprecise target characterization propagates through development

stated_failure_reason: Did not improve progression-free survival in colorectal cancer
mechanistic_assessment: Tumors developed resistance to VEGFR blockade by switching to alternative angiogenic pathways including FGF PDGF and angiopoietin. Mouse xenograft models did not show this resistance as tumor vasculature is less mature.
ontology_category: B3 - Compensatory angiogenic pathways activated upon target blockade
notes: Anti-angiogenic resistance via pathway switching is now well established but was underappreciated at time of trial

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 confirmatory trial showed no survival benefit and increased early deaths
mechanistic_assessment: CD33 expressed on both leukemia cells and normal bone marrow progenitors. Toxin delivery caused unacceptable normal tissue damage. Preclinical models did not adequately represent normal bone marrow toxicity at clinical doses.
preclinical_model_used: AML cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: F2 - Target expressed on normal tissue with toxicity underrepresented in model
notes: Later reapproved at lower dose — confirms target validity but initial dosing was wrong

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 trials did not meet primary endpoint of lupus disease activity reduction
mechanistic_assessment: Lupus is highly heterogeneous. MRL/lpr mouse model develops lupus through specific Fas gene mutation not representative of human lupus diversity. Drug may work in BAFF-dependent subgroup never identified preclinically.
preclinical_model_used: MRL/lpr mice with Fas mutation-driven autoimmunity
ontology_category: C1 - Genetically homogeneous model misses human patient heterogeneity
notes: BAFF inhibition works in belimumab for lupus — tabalumab failure was patient stratification not target failure

stated_failure_reason: No statistically significant improvement over placebo
mechanistic_assessment: Multiple adhesion molecules drive gut inflammation — blocking ICAM-1 alone insufficient as VCAM-1 and MAdCAM-1 compensated. DSS colitis model is simple epithelial damage model that does not replicate complex immune dysregulation of human Crohn's.
preclinical_model_used: DSS colitis mouse model — chemical gut damage
ontology_category: C2 - Artificially induced model does not capture human disease mechanism
notes: DSS model is mechanistically distinct from human IBD — a systematic limitation of the field

stated_failure_reason: Did not reduce COPD exacerbations in Phase 3
mechanistic_assessment: COPD exacerbations driven by multiple inflammatory mediators. IL-1beta elevated but not primary driver in most patients. Mouse COPD models do not replicate complex neutrophil-dominated multi-cytokine human exacerbation biology.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but disease driven by multiple parallel pathways
notes: Canakinumab approved for other inflammatory indications — COPD failure was indication-specific

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 showed efficacy but discontinued due to pulmonary toxicity signal
mechanistic_assessment: GM-CSF receptor also plays role in pulmonary macrophage maintenance. Blocking caused pulmonary alveolar proteinosis in humans. Not seen in rodents because rodent pulmonary macrophage biology differs from human.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target pulmonary pathway active in humans absent in rodent model
notes: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a rare but serious signal — species difference in lung macrophage biology

stated_failure_reason: Did not achieve primary endpoint in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: Eotaxin-1 drives eosinophilic gut inflammation but most Crohn's patients have neutrophil and macrophage-dominated disease. Target valid for small subset but trial enrolled broadly.
ontology_category: E1 - Model represented wrong patient subtype with broad enrollment diluting signal
notes: Immunophenotype mismatch between preclinical model and enrolled patient population

stated_failure_reason: Did not meet primary endpoint in Phase 2b
mechanistic_assessment: IP-10 elevated in Crohn's but in context of broader interferon-gamma driven network. Blocking one T cell recruitment signal while CXCL9 and CXCL11 remained active was insufficient.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but pathway redundancy made single blockade insufficient
notes: Chemokine redundancy in T cell recruitment is a consistent obstacle for single-target approaches

stated_failure_reason: Failed to show cognitive improvement in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: Cognitive deficits of schizophrenia arise from complex dopamine and glutamate circuit dysfunction that GABA modulation cannot correct. Rodent cognition models measure different cognitive domains than working memory deficits relevant to schizophrenia.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent cognition assays including Morris water maze and novel object recognition
ontology_category: C2 - Animal cognition model does not recapitulate human schizophrenia cognitive deficit
notes: No animal model reliably predicts human antipsychotic cognitive outcomes — fundamental translational gap in psychiatry

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient antipsychotic efficacy in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: NK3 receptor modulates dopamine release but is not primary driver of psychotic symptoms. Rodent model based on amphetamine-induced hyperactivity has poor face validity for human schizophrenia.
ontology_category: C2 - Model captures pharmacological readout not human disease mechanism
notes: Amphetamine model is a surrogate for dopaminergic activity not schizophrenia pathophysiology

stated_failure_reason: Did not demonstrate antidepressant efficacy in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: Depression is heterogeneous — NMDA/glutamate pathway dysregulation may only drive a subset of cases. Animal depression models measure behavioral despair not reliably predictive of human antidepressant activity.
preclinical_model_used: Forced swim test and tail suspension test in rodents
ontology_category: C2 - Behavioral rodent model does not predict human antidepressant response
notes: Forced swim test is widely criticized as a model for antidepressant screening — high false positive rate

stated_failure_reason: Development discontinued due to liver toxicity in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: Human CYP450 enzyme metabolism of ocinaplon produced a hepatotoxic metabolite at clinical doses not replicated in rodent liver metabolism pathways.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent anxiety models and standard liver safety studies
ontology_category: F1 - Species-specific metabolic pathway produced human-specific hepatotoxin
notes: CYP450 metabolic differences between species are a systematic blind spot in preclinical safety screening

stated_failure_reason: Failed to improve ADHD symptoms vs placebo in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: Alpha-7 nAChR activation shows robust procognitive effects in rodents. Human alpha-7 receptor pharmacology and CNS distribution differ from rodents particularly in prefrontal circuits responsible for executive function.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent attention tasks with limited primate data
ontology_category: A3 - Target expression and function differs between model species and humans
notes: Species divergence in alpha-7 nAChR prefrontal distribution is well documented but field continued using rodent data

stated_failure_reason: Not advanced due to cardiovascular safety concerns
mechanistic_assessment: Combined monoamine reuptake inhibition caused cardiovascular stimulation — heart rate and blood pressure elevation — more pronounced in humans than rodents. Rodent cardiovascular physiology handles monoamine excess differently.
ontology_category: F1 - Off-target cardiovascular effects underweighted in rodent model
notes: Cardiovascular sensitivity to monoamine excess is consistently underestimated in rodent models

stated_failure_reason: FDA required more CV safety data — program halted after meta-analysis showed increased CV events
mechanistic_assessment: Dual PPAR activation caused fluid retention and cardiovascular complications not adequately captured in rodent metabolic models. Rodents handle PPAR-mediated fluid and cardiac effects differently from humans.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent diabetes models including db/db mice and Zucker rats
ontology_category: F1 - Off-target cardiovascular and fluid effects underrepresented in rodent model
notes: First of multiple dual PPAR agonist failures — class-level signal that should have informed subsequent programs

stated_failure_reason: Trial stopped early — no CV event reduction with bone fracture and heart failure signals
mechanistic_assessment: Same class problem as muraglitazar — dual PPAR agonism causes fluid retention heart failure risk and bone effects. Rodent models continued to underpredict human fluid and cardiac sensitivity despite prior class failures.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent models with some primate data
ontology_category: F1 - Class-level off-target toxicity with model systematically underpredicting human cardiac sensitivity
notes: Second major dual PPAR failure — class should have been deprioritized after muraglitazar

stated_failure_reason: FDA placed clinical hold due to deaths in Phase 2/3 trials
mechanistic_assessment: MetAP2 inhibition caused thrombotic events. Not seen in preclinical animal studies because coagulation cascade response to MetAP2 inhibition differs between species. Mechanism connecting MetAP2 to thrombosis not characterized preclinically.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent obesity models including DIO mice
ontology_category: F1 - Off-target thrombotic pathway active in humans not in rodent model
notes: Fatal adverse events — most severe consequence of species-specific off-target toxicity failure

stated_failure_reason: Did not reduce mortality or organ failure in Phase 2 sepsis trial
mechanistic_assessment: Neutrophil recruitment in sepsis is double-edged — early recruitment essential for pathogen clearance late recruitment causes organ damage. Blocking neutrophil adhesion universally impaired bacterial clearance while failing to reduce inflammation. Mouse sepsis models do not capture this timing complexity.
preclinical_model_used: LPS-induced sepsis mouse models and cecal ligation and puncture
ontology_category: C2 - Sepsis model does not capture timing complexity of human septic progression
notes: Neutrophil biology in sepsis is bidirectional — broad blockade fails because it removes beneficial early function

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 trial failed — no reduction in 28-day mortality
mechanistic_assessment: TLR4 blocks the LPS receptor — mechanistically sound for gram-negative sepsis. But sepsis mortality driven by complex multi-pathway immune dysregulation. After initial LPS hit the downstream inflammatory network runs independently. Blocking TLR4 after the fact is insufficient.
ontology_category: E3 - Intervention point too late — model does not capture disease stage at time of treatment
notes: TLR4 antagonism may still be valid if given prophylactically — timing is the key variable

stated_failure_reason: Withdrawn — Phase 4 confirmatory trial showed no mortality benefit and increased bleeding
mechanistic_assessment: Initial Phase 3 showed benefit in severe sepsis. Later trials in broader populations showed no benefit and harm. The subgroup with protein C deficiency who benefited was buried in broader enrollment.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent sepsis models and non-human primate models
ontology_category: E1 - Patient heterogeneity — benefit in subgroup diluted by broad enrollment
notes: Regulatory approval based on heterogeneous population — benefit was real in a specific subgroup

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 missed primary endpoint — no significant improvement in 6-minute walk test
mechanistic_assessment: Drug mechanism biologically valid. Failure partly patient selection — only nonsense mutation patients should respond which is 13 percent of DMD. Primary endpoint insufficiently sensitive for slowly progressing disease. mdx mice more severe than human patients overestimating effect size.
preclinical_model_used: mdx mice — dystrophin-deficient with more severe phenotype than human disease course
ontology_category: C2 - Animal model more severe than human disease overestimates treatment effect size
notes: Endpoint sensitivity failure combined with patient selection — two independent problems compounding each other

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed to show significant improvement in respiratory function
mechanistic_assessment: Oxidative stress is a secondary contributor to DMD — primary problem is structural membrane damage from absent dystrophin. Addressing oxidative stress alone in a disease with structural primary pathology was insufficient.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid for secondary pathway but primary disease mechanism not addressed
notes: Secondary pathway targeting without addressing primary structural defect — insufficient in any disease with major structural pathology

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 failed to reduce liver fibrosis in NASH or primary sclerosing cholangitis
mechanistic_assessment: LOXL2 elevated in fibrotic liver and lung. But fibrosis driven by multiple parallel crosslinking enzymes and ECM-remodeling pathways. Blocking LOXL2 alone insufficient — other LOX family members and matrix metalloproteinases continued driving fibrosis.
preclinical_model_used: CCl4-induced liver fibrosis mouse model and BDL model
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but disease driven by redundant parallel pathways
notes: LOXL2 antibody approach may have failed partly due to inability to penetrate fibrotic tissue — delivery may be co-factor

stated_failure_reason: FDA rejected approval — concerns about worsening joint destruction in subset of patients
mechanistic_assessment: Nerve growth factor drives pain signaling. Blocking it relieved pain effectively. But NGF also supports joint tissue maintenance — blocking it accelerated joint destruction in a subset of patients. This destructive joint effect was not adequately predicted from animal pain models.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent nerve injury and inflammatory pain models
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target joint maintenance pathway active in humans underweighted in animal pain models
notes: Pain relief was confirmed but joint destruction signal was a genuine surprise — NGF trophic functions in joint tissue undercharacterized

stated_failure_reason: Withdrawn from market — severe hepatotoxicity including liver failure deaths
mechanistic_assessment: Thrombin inhibition was mechanistically valid. However ximelagatran produced a hepatotoxic metabolite through human-specific liver metabolism not replicated in rodent or primate safety studies. Short-term liver enzyme elevation resolved in animals and early human studies masking long-term hepatotoxicity risk.
ontology_category: F1 - Species-specific hepatic metabolism produced human-specific toxin
notes: First oral direct thrombin inhibitor withdrawn — human CYP metabolism produced toxic metabolite invisible in standard preclinical safety battery

stated_failure_reason: Failed to show antidepressant efficacy in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: NK1 receptor blockade reduces stress responses in rodent models convincingly. Human depression involves complex monoaminergic and neuroplasticity deficits that substance P modulation cannot address. Rodent stress models have poor predictive validity for human antidepressant response.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent stress and learned helplessness models
ontology_category: C2 - Rodent stress model does not predict human antidepressant response
notes: High-profile failure — generated significant discussion about validity of rodent antidepressant models

stated_failure_reason: Early Phase 2 programs showed insufficient efficacy and GI tolerability issues
mechanistic_assessment: PDE4 inhibition reduces inflammation in COPD — mechanistically valid. But nausea vomiting and diarrhea from PDE4 inhibition in the gut were severe in humans and not adequately predicted from animal tolerability studies. Rodents tolerate PDE4 inhibition better than humans gastrointestinally.
ontology_category: F1 - GI tolerability of PDE4 inhibition underestimated in rodent models
notes: Later approved at lower dose with better tolerability management — dose finding was the key

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy in Phase 2 RA trial
mechanistic_assessment: CCR2 and CCR5 drive macrophage and T cell recruitment to inflamed joints. Blocking them was rational. But RA is driven by multiple redundant chemokine recruitment pathways — blocking CCR2/5 alone while other chemokines remained active was insufficient.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but disease driven by redundant chemokine recruitment pathways
notes: Maraviroc approved for HIV — CCR5 inhibition valid in HIV context but insufficient as sole target in complex autoimmune disease

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 failed — insufficient efficacy with liver toxicity signal
mechanistic_assessment: p38 MAPK drives TNF and IL-6 production in inflammatory cells. Blocking it was rational. But p38 MAPK is also essential for many normal cellular stress responses. Chronic blockade caused hepatotoxicity not predicted from short-term animal studies. Also disease rebounded via alternative inflammatory kinase pathways.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target hepatic stress pathway disrupted in humans
notes: Multiple p38 inhibitors failed — class problem with chronic hepatotoxicity not visible in short-duration animal studies

stated_failure_reason: No improvement in cancer survival; severe musculoskeletal toxicity
mechanistic_assessment: Matrix metalloproteinases were thought to be purely destructive in cancer invasion. But MMPs also play essential roles in normal tissue remodeling wound healing and immune function. Broad MMP inhibition caused musculoskeletal syndrome — joint pain and fibrosis — not predicted from animal studies. Also tumors used alternative invasion pathways.
ontology_category: A1 - Target plays essential normal tissue maintenance roles underappreciated preclinically
notes: Entire MMP inhibitor class failed — fundamental misunderstanding of MMP biology in normal tissue homeostasis

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient response rate in unselected colorectal cancer population
mechanistic_assessment: EGFR inhibition works in KRAS wild-type colorectal cancer. But early trials enrolled all comers including KRAS-mutant patients who cannot respond because downstream RAS signaling bypasses EGFR. Diluted the signal from true responders. Preclinical cell line work did not adequately model KRAS mutation status.
preclinical_model_used: Colorectal cancer cell lines mixed KRAS status
ontology_category: E2 - Critical responder biomarker (KRAS wild-type status) not identified preclinically
notes: Later succeeded when restricted to KRAS wild-type patients — textbook patient stratification failure and subsequent success

stated_failure_reason: No significant efficacy in solid tumor Phase 2 trials
mechanistic_assessment: Flavopiridol is a pan-CDK inhibitor not specific to CDK4/6. Broad CDK inhibition caused severe toxicity because CDKs are essential for normal cell cycle in all dividing tissues. Later selective CDK4/6 inhibitors succeeded — the problem was selectivity not the target.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: A2 - Drug inhibited wrong CDK family members — mechanism not specific to intended target
notes: Failure of pan-CDK inhibitors led to selective CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib etc) which succeeded — target was right drug was wrong

stated_failure_reason: Trials terminated — no benefit and potential harm in heart failure
mechanistic_assessment: TNF-alpha is elevated in heart failure and was thought to drive cardiac inflammation. Blocking TNF worked in rheumatoid arthritis. But in heart failure TNF serves a cardioprotective role — it helps cardiomyocytes survive injury. Blocking it removed this protection. Mouse heart failure models did not capture this cardioprotective TNF function.
ontology_category: B3 - Target plays opposing roles in different disease contexts — protective not harmful in heart
notes: Canonical example of same target succeeding in one disease (RA) and failing harmfully in another (heart failure) — context-dependent biology

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 showed trend but Phase 3 failed — no improvement in heart failure outcomes
mechanistic_assessment: Endothelin-1 is elevated in heart failure and drives vasoconstriction. Blocking endothelin receptors reduces vascular resistance — rational. But endothelin also plays a role in cardiac adaptation to stress. Broad blockade of ET-A and ET-B receptors interfered with compensatory cardiac mechanisms. Mouse heart failure models showed hemodynamic benefit without capturing long-term adaptive biology.
ontology_category: B3 - Target plays adaptive compensatory role in human heart failure context
notes: Bosentan succeeded in pulmonary arterial hypertension — same drug different disease context worked because PAH lacks the compensatory cardiac mechanism problem

stated_failure_reason: Early Phase 2 programs showed insufficient weight loss
mechanistic_assessment: 5-HT2c receptor activation suppresses appetite via hypothalamic pathways. Works in rodent obesity models. Human appetite regulation involves more complex hedonic and cognitive circuits than rodent hypothalamic satiety models capture. Effect size in humans smaller than predicted from animal models.
ontology_category: C2 - Rodent appetite model overestimates effect size of hypothalamic appetite suppression in humans
notes: Later approved (lorcaserin) at approved doses but withdrawn for cancer risk — target had a long difficult development history

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 halted — 6 percent of patients developed meningoencephalitis brain inflammation
mechanistic_assessment: Active vaccination against amyloid-beta generated T cell response against brain tissue. Preclinical mouse immunization studies showed amyloid clearance without inflammation. Human immune responses to amyloid vaccination generated pathological T cell-mediated brain inflammation not seen in transgenic mice because mouse immune systems respond to human amyloid differently.
ontology_category: C2 - Mouse immune response to human amyloid does not predict human T cell-mediated neuroinflammation
notes: First active immunotherapy for AD — failure led to passive antibody approach. T cell response to amyloid was not modeled in transgenic mice

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2b failed to slow motor progression in early Parkinson's
mechanistic_assessment: Alpha-synuclein aggregation drives Parkinson's neurodegeneration. Antibody cleared alpha-synuclein. But like amyloid in AD clearing the protein may not halt already-triggered neurodegeneration. Also enrolled patients may already have had irreversible dopaminergic neuron loss.
ontology_category: B2 - Biomarker cleared but neurodegenerative cascade already irreversible at enrollment
notes: Mirrors Alzheimer's amyloid failures — protein clearance without functional recovery is an emerging pattern across neurodegeneration

stated_failure_reason: No cognitive benefit in Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: VEGF promotes neurogenesis and blood-brain barrier function — thought to be neuroprotective. Animal models of cognitive decline showed VEGF benefit. But human AD is too advanced by symptomatic stage and VEGF delivery to brain was insufficient in clinical formulations.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent cognitive decline and ischemia models
ontology_category: E3 - Enrolled patients too late in disease — neuroprotection cannot reverse established neurodegeneration
notes: VEGF neuroprotection may be valid as prevention not treatment — disease stage at intervention is the key variable

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2b failed to improve behavioral symptoms in Fragile X
mechanistic_assessment: mGluR5 hypothesis for Fragile X was well supported — FMR1 protein normally suppresses mGluR5 signaling and its absence causes overactivation. Mouse Fmr1 knockout model showed robust behavioral rescue with mGluR5 blockers. Human trials showed no benefit. Mouse behavioral tests (open field marble burying) measure very different behavioral dimensions than human Fragile X symptoms.
ontology_category: C2 - Mouse behavioral assays do not map to human Fragile X symptom domains
notes: High-profile failure — mGluR5 hypothesis was scientifically strong but mouse behavioral tests were not predictive of human outcomes

stated_failure_reason: No cognitive benefit in Phase 2 AD trials
mechanistic_assessment: PDE5 inhibition raises cGMP and was thought to enhance synaptic plasticity and memory. Works in rodent memory models. Human AD cognition involves structural neurodegeneration not addressable by synaptic modulation alone. Also brain penetration of PDE5 inhibitors at safe doses was insufficient.
ontology_category: C2 - Rodent synaptic plasticity model does not capture human neurodegeneration context
notes: PDE5 inhibition may enhance normal cognition — does not address structural neurodegeneration of established AD

stated_failure_reason: No significant HbA1c reduction — pancreatic toxicity signal
mechanistic_assessment: BACE2 was thought to regulate pancreatic beta cell function. Inhibiting it was hypothesized to improve insulin secretion. But BACE2 and BACE1 share overlapping substrate cleavage — BACE2 inhibitors also affected BACE1 substrates causing cognitive and pancreatic side effects. Rodent BACE2 biology differs from human.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target BACE1 substrate cleavage disrupted in humans
notes: BACE1/BACE2 substrate overlap is a fundamental problem for selective inhibition — species differences complicate this further

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed to slow Alzheimer's progression
mechanistic_assessment: RAGE receptor drives inflammation and oxidative stress in diabetic complications and was hypothesized to drive neuroinflammation in AD. Animal models showed benefit. Human Phase 3 failed. RAGE has many ligands and pathways in human disease making single blockade insufficient. Also enrolled patients had established AD — too late for anti-inflammatory neuroprotection.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent diabetic complication and transgenic AD models
ontology_category: E3 - Enrolled patients at wrong disease stage combined with pathway redundancy
notes: Anti-RAGE approach rational as prevention — failed as treatment of established neurodegeneration

stated_failure_reason: Withdrawn — severe psychiatric side effects including suicidality
mechanistic_assessment: CB1 receptor blockade in the brain reduces appetite and body weight effectively. Works in rodent obesity models. But CB1 receptors are also essential for mood regulation and emotional processing. Blocking them caused depression anxiety and suicidality in humans — psychiatric effects not adequately captured in rodent behavioral models.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target CNS mood regulation pathway active in humans underweighted in rodent models
notes: Weight loss was confirmed — psychiatric toxicity was the failure. Rodent mood models do not adequately capture human psychiatric adverse effects of CB1 blockade

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy in obesity; later cachexia programs also mixed
mechanistic_assessment: Ghrelin receptor activation stimulates appetite — blocking it should reduce appetite. Works in rodent feeding models. Human appetite regulation involves more complex behavioral and hedonic components. Also compensatory appetite signals upregulated when ghrelin blocked. Rodent feeding models do not capture human eating behavior complexity.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent feeding and body weight models
ontology_category: C2 - Rodent feeding model overestimates human appetite suppression from ghrelin blockade
notes: Ghrelin agonism (not antagonism) later showed utility in cancer cachexia — different indication same target

stated_failure_reason: No clinical benefit in inflammatory disease Phase 2 trials
mechanistic_assessment: NF-kB drives inflammatory gene expression and is a rational target. But NF-kB is also essential for normal immune responses cell survival and development. Broad NF-kB blockade caused immunosuppression and toxicity. Disease continued via NF-kB independent inflammatory pathways. No animal model captured human inflammatory disease complexity.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but essential for normal immunity — blockade causes immunosuppression
notes: NF-kB is too central to normal immunity to block broadly — selective pathway approaches needed

stated_failure_reason: Withdrawn — excess cardiovascular events in long-term cancer prevention trial
mechanistic_assessment: COX-2 drives prostaglandin production that promotes tumor growth — rational for cancer prevention. But COX-2 also produces prostacyclin which protects against thrombosis. Long-term COX-2 blockade tipped the thromboxane/prostacyclin balance toward thrombosis causing heart attacks. Short-duration animal models did not capture this long-term cardiovascular imbalance.
ontology_category: F1 - Long-term cardiovascular effect of prostaglandin imbalance not visible in short-duration animal studies
notes: One of largest drug withdrawals in history — prostacyclin/thromboxane imbalance was predictable but ignored

stated_failure_reason: Development halted — severe hyperthermia in humans
mechanistic_assessment: TRPV1 is a pain and temperature sensor. Blocking it reduces pain in animal models effectively. But TRPV1 is also essential for normal body temperature regulation in humans — blocking it causes hyperthermia (dangerously elevated body temperature). Rodent TRPV1 blockade causes much milder hyperthermia than in humans due to species differences in thermoregulatory physiology.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent pain models — formalin test and hot plate
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target thermoregulatory pathway much more sensitive to TRPV1 blockade in humans than rodents
notes: Entire TRPV1 antagonist class failed on hyperthermia — fundamental species difference in thermoregulation through TRPV1

stated_failure_reason: No significant pain relief in Phase 2 human pain trials
mechanistic_assessment: Nav1.7 mutations that abolish its function cause congenital insensitivity to pain in humans — validating the target genetically. But pharmacological blockade of Nav1.7 did not reproduce the pain relief of genetic loss. Drug penetration to peripheral neurons insufficient and other Nav channels compensated acutely for Nav1.7 blockade in ways genetic loss during development does not.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent Nav1.7 knockout and pain models
ontology_category: B3 - Genetic validation did not translate to pharmacological validation — compensatory Nav channels
notes: Genetic vs pharmacological target validation discrepancy — important distinction for Terracotta ontology

stated_failure_reason: Early Phase 2 concerns about injection site reactions and durability
mechanistic_assessment: PCSK9 inhibition lowers LDL — target is well validated. Early programs had formulation and delivery issues. Not a pure target failure — delivery and formulation problems. Later programs (evolocumab alirocumab) succeeded with better antibody engineering.
ontology_category: D3 - Formulation and delivery not adequate — not a target failure
notes: Including as example where early failure led to successful refinement — target was right execution was wrong

company_or_program: Various gamma-secretase inhibitor programs for T-ALL
stated_failure_reason: GI toxicity prevented dose escalation to therapeutic levels
mechanistic_assessment: Notch is hyperactivated in T-ALL through NOTCH1 mutations. Blocking Notch with gamma-secretase inhibitors should work. But as with Alzheimer's programs gamma-secretase also cleaves many other substrates causing severe GI toxicity from intestinal goblet cell metaplasia. Therapeutic dose was impossible to achieve without unacceptable GI damage.
preclinical_model_used: T-ALL cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target GI Notch pathway disrupted at therapeutic doses in humans
notes: Same gamma-secretase off-target Notch problem as semagacestat — confirms A1 as a robust ontology node

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 failed to improve survival in hepatocellular carcinoma
mechanistic_assessment: TGF-beta drives tumor immunosuppression and cancer cell invasion. Blocking it was rational. But TGF-beta also plays tumor suppressive roles in early cancer and normal tissue homeostatic roles. Broad TGF-beta blockade in advanced cancer activated both anti-tumor and pro-tumor effects simultaneously. Mouse xenograft models used immunodeficient animals and could not capture immunological complexity.
preclinical_model_used: HCC xenograft models in immunodeficient mice
ontology_category: C3 - Immunodeficient model cannot capture dual tumor-suppressive and pro-tumorigenic TGF-beta roles
notes: TGF-beta is bidirectional in cancer — tumor suppressive early and pro-tumorigenic late. Model immunodeficiency masks this complexity

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed to improve outcomes when combined with pembrolizumab in melanoma
mechanistic_assessment: IDO1 metabolizes tryptophan to suppress T cell activity — blocking it should enhance anti-tumor immunity. Phase 2 single arm data looked promising. Phase 3 with pembrolizumab showed no benefit. Phase 2 signal was likely inflated by pembrolizumab alone in uncontrolled trial design. Mouse tumor models showed IDO1 blockade benefit but mouse IDO1 biology differs from human.
ontology_category: E1 - Phase 2 signal was false positive from uncontrolled design — pembrolizumab alone drove the response
notes: One of largest Phase 3 failures in immuno-oncology — uncontrolled Phase 2 design gave misleading signal that drove massive Phase 3 investment

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 failed for inflammatory indications — serious infection rate
mechanistic_assessment: PI3K-delta is highly expressed in immune cells and its inhibition reduces inflammatory signaling. Works in RA and IBD animal models. But PI3K-delta is also essential for regulatory T cell function — blocking it paradoxically caused autoimmune colitis and serious infections by removing immune regulation. Mouse immune models did not capture this regulatory T cell dependency.
ontology_category: A1 - Off-target regulatory T cell pathway dependent on PI3K-delta disrupted in humans
notes: Idelalisib approved for blood cancer — failed in inflammatory disease because inflammatory vs cancer immune context differs critically

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient response rate in unselected bladder cancer population
mechanistic_assessment: FGFR mutations drive bladder cancer in a specific subset of patients. Early trials did not select for FGFR mutation status and enrolled all bladder cancer patients. The 20 percent with FGFR mutations had responses but the 80 percent without diluted the signal to statistical noise.
preclinical_model_used: Bladder cancer cell lines mixed FGFR status
ontology_category: E2 - Responder biomarker (FGFR mutation status) not used for patient selection
notes: Later succeeded when restricted to FGFR-mutant patients (erdafitinib) — mirrors EGFR/KRAS story in colorectal cancer

company_or_program: Various early trastuzumab gastric cancer programs
stated_failure_reason: Insufficient overall response in unselected gastric cancer population
mechanistic_assessment: HER2 amplification drives gastric cancer in about 20 percent of patients. Early programs enrolled unselected gastric cancer patients. HER2-negative patients could not respond. Signal from HER2-positive patients diluted by non-responders. Later succeeded when restricted to HER2-positive patients.
ontology_category: E2 - Responder biomarker (HER2 amplification status) not used for patient selection
notes: Trastuzumab now approved in HER2-positive gastric cancer — patient selection failure not target failure

stated_failure_reason: No mortality reduction in Phase 2 sepsis trials
mechanistic_assessment: C5a complement activation drives excessive inflammation in sepsis. Blocking C5aR reduces organ damage in animal models. But in human sepsis complement activation occurs alongside many other inflammatory cascades. Blocking C5a alone was insufficient. Mouse sepsis models show higher C5a pathway dependence than complex human septic cascades.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but sepsis driven by redundant inflammatory pathways beyond C5a
notes: Complement as drug target in sepsis has been tried many times — pathway redundancy is consistent obstacle

indication: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
stated_failure_reason: No improvement in outcomes in HFpEF — drugs effective in HFrEF failed
mechanistic_assessment: Renin-angiotensin system blockade works in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. HFpEF was assumed similar. But HFpEF has different pathophysiology — driven by diastolic stiffness inflammation and metabolic dysfunction rather than neurohormonal overactivation. Mouse heart failure models predominantly model systolic dysfunction not diastolic HFpEF biology.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent systolic heart failure models (LAD ligation)
ontology_category: C2 - Model recapitulates wrong heart failure subtype — systolic not diastolic
notes: HFpEF remains one of largest unmet needs in cardiology — model inadequacy is central to slow progress

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy signal in early Phase 2 programs before dose optimization
mechanistic_assessment: D3 receptor blockade was hypothesized to improve negative symptoms of schizophrenia beyond D2 blockade alone. Animal models of negative symptoms (social withdrawal anhedonia) showed benefit. But negative symptoms in humans involve complex prefrontal-limbic circuit dysfunction that D3 modulation alone cannot address. Effect size much smaller than animal models predicted.
preclinical_model_used: Rodent social interaction and anhedonia models
ontology_category: C2 - Rodent negative symptom models overestimate human D3 receptor contribution to negative symptoms
notes: Cariprazine eventually approved at optimized doses — not pure failure but highlights effect size overestimation from animal models

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient mobilization and anti-tumor activity in early Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: CXCR4 tethers myeloma cells to bone marrow niche protecting them from chemotherapy. Disrupting CXCR4-CXCL12 axis should mobilize and sensitize myeloma cells. Works in mouse myeloma models. But human bone marrow niche interactions involve multiple redundant adhesion and retention mechanisms — CXCR4 alone was insufficient to fully displace myeloma cells from the niche.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but bone marrow niche retention involves redundant parallel mechanisms
notes: CXCR4 inhibition (plerixafor) approved for stem cell mobilization — works for that narrow indication but insufficient alone for myeloma treatment

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 bone pain endpoint not met — bone protection confirmed but pain relief insufficient
mechanistic_assessment: RANKL drives osteoclast activity causing bone destruction in metastasis. Denosumab prevents bone destruction effectively. But bone metastasis pain involves multiple mechanisms including nerve sensitization tumor-derived pain mediators and inflammatory cytokines beyond bone destruction alone. Preventing bone damage did not adequately reduce pain.
ontology_category: D1 - Biomarker (bone resorption markers) improved but downstream pain mechanism unaffected
notes: Denosumab approved for skeletal events — bone protection confirmed but pain is driven by additional mechanisms beyond bone destruction

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 failed — disease worsened in some patients on secukinumab
mechanistic_assessment: IL-17A drives inflammation in psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis. Blocking it was tried in Crohn's disease. But IL-17A plays a protective role in gut mucosal immunity — blocking it paradoxically worsened gut inflammation in Crohn's patients by removing mucosal defense. Mouse gut models did not capture this protective IL-17A role in human intestinal immunity.
ontology_category: B3 - Target plays opposing protective role in gut that animal model did not capture
notes: Secukinumab approved in psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis — same drug different disease context — gut protective IL-17A role is human-specific

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed primary histological endpoint — safety concerns with pruritus and LDL elevation
mechanistic_assessment: FXR activation reduces liver fat and fibrosis in NASH animal models. Obeticholic acid confirmed FXR engagement. But FXR activation also reduces bile acid synthesis which increases LDL cholesterol. In NASH patients who already have cardiovascular risk this LDL elevation was problematic. Mouse NASH models do not recapitulate human cardiovascular comorbidity context.
preclinical_model_used: Mouse NASH models (NASH diet and STAM models)
ontology_category: D1 - Biomarker improved but off-target LDL elevation clinically unacceptable in patient population with high CV risk
notes: NASH field has had multiple failures — human disease complexity and comorbidity context not captured in mouse dietary models

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed to improve liver fibrosis in advanced NASH
mechanistic_assessment: ASK1 drives oxidative stress-induced liver cell death and fibrosis. Blocking it reduced liver injury markers in early studies. Phase 3 failed to show fibrosis improvement. Multiple parallel fibrosis pathways (TGF-beta PDGF stellate cell activation) continued driving fibrosis when ASK1 was blocked alone. Mouse NASH fibrosis models show higher ASK1 pathway dependence.
preclinical_model_used: Mouse NASH fibrosis models (CCl4 and dietary)
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but liver fibrosis driven by redundant parallel pathways beyond ASK1
notes: Multiple NASH drug failures share same root — liver fibrosis is driven by many parallel pathways and single target blockade is insufficient

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient anti-fibrotic efficacy in Phase 2b
mechanistic_assessment: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition reduces liver fat by blocking de novo lipogenesis. Confirmed fat reduction. But NASH fibrosis is driven by stellate cell activation inflammatory mediators and oxidative stress — reducing fat alone without addressing fibrogenic pathways was insufficient. Mouse NASH models overrepresent lipogenic pathway contribution to fibrosis.
ontology_category: B3 - Reducing lipid burden insufficient without addressing fibrogenic inflammation
notes: Third NASH failure following similar pattern — fibrosis pathway redundancy is the consistent obstacle in this disease area

stated_failure_reason: Development halted — severe skin and eye toxicity in humans
mechanistic_assessment: SCD1 is a fatty acid desaturase enzyme involved in fat metabolism. Blocking it reduces obesity and metabolic syndrome in rodents. But SCD1 is essential for sebaceous gland and meibomian gland function in humans — blocking it caused severe skin dryness and eye surface problems not seen in rodents because rodent skin and eye biology differs substantially.
ontology_category: F1 - Species-specific skin and eye gland SCD1 dependency caused human-specific toxicity
notes: Entire SCD1 inhibitor class failed on skin and eye toxicity — fundamental species difference in SCD1 dependency in skin glands

company_or_program: Various early GLP-1 programs for NASH
stated_failure_reason: Phase 2 showed insufficient liver fibrosis improvement despite fat reduction
mechanistic_assessment: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce liver fat effectively. But NASH progression and fibrosis involves inflammatory and stellate cell mechanisms beyond lipid accumulation. Fat reduction alone was insufficient to improve fibrosis endpoints. Mouse NASH models often improve fully with fat reduction alone — human disease is more driven by independent fibrogenic pathways.
preclinical_model_used: Mouse dietary NASH models (MCD and HFD)
ontology_category: B3 - Lipid reduction target insufficient — fibrosis driven by independent parallel pathways
notes: Later higher-dose GLP-1 programs showed more promise — dose and fibrosis endpoint sensitivity were key variables

stated_failure_reason: Phase 3 failed — increased deaths in MET-low patients
mechanistic_assessment: c-MET amplification drives gastric cancer in a subset of patients. Early Phase 2 selected for MET-high patients and showed benefit. Phase 3 enrolled broader MET-positive population including MET-low patients. MET-low patients may have been harmed by the antibody through immune-related mechanisms. Preclinical models used only MET-high cell lines not capturing MET-low patient biology.
ontology_category: E1 - Broad enrollment of MET-positive patients included MET-low patients who were potentially harmed
notes: MET-low patients being harmed was a critical unexpected finding — biomarker threshold definition was too loose

stated_failure_reason: Development halted — severe gastrointestinal toxicity at therapeutic doses
mechanistic_assessment: Wnt pathway is hyperactivated in colorectal cancer — rational target. But Wnt is also essential for intestinal crypt stem cell renewal in normal gut. Blocking Wnt in tumor cells also blocked normal gut stem cell maintenance causing severe GI toxicity. No therapeutic window possible because tumor and normal intestinal cells have equivalent Wnt dependency.
preclinical_model_used: Colorectal cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: F2 - Target essential for normal intestinal stem cell maintenance — no therapeutic window
notes: Wnt pathway inhibition in colorectal cancer is theoretically impossible without GI toxicity — normal gut Wnt dependency creates an unavoidable therapeutic window problem

stated_failure_reason: Phase 2b mixed results — efficacy in subset but broad enrollment diluted signal
mechanistic_assessment: OX40/OX40L drives Th2 inflammatory responses in atopic dermatitis. Works in animal allergy models. Human atopic dermatitis is immunologically heterogeneous — Th2-dominant patients responded but Th1 and mixed-phenotype patients did not. Preclinical models used Th2-skewed mouse allergy models not capturing human disease heterogeneity.
ontology_category: C1 - Th2-skewed model not representative of full spectrum of human atopic dermatitis immunophenotypes
notes: Later programs showed better results with patient stratification — Th2-dominant subgroup identification improved outcomes

company_or_program: Various early CGRP programs for cluster headache
stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy in episodic cluster headache Phase 2
mechanistic_assessment: CGRP drives migraine pain — CGRP inhibitors work in migraine. Cluster headache was assumed to share the same mechanism. But cluster headache involves hypothalamic activation and trigeminal autonomic features that are distinct from migraine CGRP pathways. Animal trigeminal pain models do not distinguish between migraine and cluster headache mechanisms.
ontology_category: C2 - Animal model does not distinguish migraine vs cluster headache pain mechanisms
notes: CGRP inhibitors work in migraine — cluster headache involves additional hypothalamic mechanisms beyond CGRP

stated_failure_reason: Insufficient efficacy signal in Phase 2 — tolerability concerns
mechanistic_assessment: NLRP3 drives IL-1beta production in gout crystals. Animal gout models showed benefit. In humans NLRP3 is one of multiple inflammasome complexes active in gout — other inflammasomes (NLRP1 AIM2) compensated when NLRP3 was blocked. Also NLRP3 plays important roles in normal pathogen defense — chronic blockade increased infection risk.
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but parallel inflammasome pathways compensate in human gout
notes: NLRP3 inhibition promising in early data but human inflammasome redundancy limits single-target approach

stated_failure_reason: No significant tumor responses in Phase 2 solid tumor trials
mechanistic_assessment: Eg5 kinesin is essential for mitotic spindle formation — blocking it should arrest cancer cell division. Works in cancer cell lines and animal models. But clinical responses were very limited. Solid tumors have heterogeneous cell cycle states and many cells are not actively dividing at time of treatment. Also drug delivery to solid tumor cores was inadequate.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: E1 - Unselected tumors had low mitotic fraction — insufficient tumor cells actively dividing to show response
notes: Mitotic index of solid tumors much lower than cell lines — cell line models systematically overestimate activity of cell cycle targeted drugs in solid tumors

company_or_program: Various early HDAC inhibitor programs for solid tumors
stated_failure_reason: No significant efficacy in solid tumor Phase 2 trials despite hematologic malignancy activity
mechanistic_assessment: HDAC inhibitors work well in hematologic malignancies (cutaneous T cell lymphoma). In solid tumors failed to show efficacy. Solid tumor microenvironment has dense stroma limiting drug penetration. Also solid tumor cells have different epigenetic dependencies than liquid tumor cells. Cell line models used for solid tumors do not capture tumor microenvironment and stromal barriers.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: C3 - Immunodeficient xenograft model lacks stromal microenvironment context of solid tumors
notes: HDAC inhibitors work in liquid tumors — solid tumor failure reflects stromal penetration and epigenetic dependency differences not visible in standard xenograft models

stated_failure_reason: No significant tumor responses in Phase 2 solid tumor trials
mechanistic_assessment: Survivin is an anti-apoptotic protein overexpressed in many cancers. Blocking it was hypothesized to trigger cancer cell death. Works in cancer cell lines. But survivin inhibition in vivo caused rapid upregulation of other IAP family members (XIAP cIAP1) that compensated for survivin loss. Cell line models showed cleaner survivin dependency than heterogeneous patient tumors with redundant IAP pathway protection.
preclinical_model_used: Cancer cell lines and xenograft models
ontology_category: B3 - Target valid but IAP family redundancy compensates for survivin inhibition in patient tumors
notes: IAP family redundancy is a consistent obstacle — same pathway compensation problem as Bcl-2 family
